_about: Global game settings. Times are in seconds, rates are per minute. Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored by the game.
_difficulties: How hard a new game is. The player picks one on the title screen. Each may change the starting coins (startCoins), the income the island earns with no residents (baseIncomePerMinute), and every resident's tax (taxMultiplier: 1 is unchanged, 1.1 is a tenth more). Anything left out stays as it is below. 'normal' changes nothing, so it is the game as balanced.

easy.name: Easy
easy.about: More coins to start, and more income. A bad start is forgiven.

normal.name: Normal
normal.about: The game as it was balanced.

hard.name: Hard
hard.about: Fewer coins to start, and less tax. Mistakes cost more.

_scenarios: Games with their own island, start and goal, offered on the title screen. A scenario may set: seed (the island), startCoins, startGoods, baseIncomePerMinute, win (tier and residents), milestones (goals after the win; an empty list means none), workforce (base and perResident), secondIslandOpen (true: the second island is open from the start, not only after the win), and medals (gold and silver, in game minutes: finish within the time to earn the medal, and any later finish is bronze). Anything left out stays as in the standard game. Scenarios never change the standard game or its saved games.

fishing-village.name: Fishing village
fishing-village.about: A gentle one. No upgrades needed: fill the shore with houses and keep them in fish.

weavers-guild.name: The weavers' guild
weavers-guild.about: A well-off start, and a town that wants fine cloth. Go straight for Artisans, and mind who staffs the workshops.

vintners.name: The vintners
vintners.about: The second island is open from the start, and the town wants wine: without it an Artisan house holds only 8. Settle early, ship the grapes home, and keep some wood and planks back for the town.

short-handed.name: Short-handed
short-handed.about: Few hands on this island. The first crew is larger, but only 1 resident in 4 works. Keep houses ahead of workshops.

_undoSeconds: How long, in game seconds, your last action can be taken back with Undo. 0 switches Undo off.
_undoSteps: How many of your last actions Undo can take back, one after another, newest first. Each still only within undoSeconds of when you did it. 1 is the last action only.

economy._incomeIntervalSeconds: How often taxes, base income and upkeep are settled.
economy._baseIncomePerMinute: Coins the island earns with no residents at all. This is the safety net that stops a player getting stuck at zero.
economy._demolishRefundRatio: Share of a building's cost (coins and goods) returned on demolish, rounded down.

_workforce: Staff for the producing buildings. Each producer linked to a warehouse needs the 'staff' set for it in buildings.json. The town has 'base' staff to begin with, plus 'perResident' for every resident (0.5 means one in two residents works). A town with fewer staff than it needs works slower, every producer by the same share: 30 staff where 40 are needed is 75% speed. Remove this whole entry to switch the rule off.
_carts: Finished goods travel by road. A producer puts what it makes in its yard, which holds 'yard' units. A cart from the nearest warehouse by road fetches them, 'load' at a time, taking 'ticksPerTile' ticks (tenths of a second) for each road tile each way. A producer more than 'reachTiles' road tiles from every warehouse is never collected. How many carts a warehouse keeps is in buildings.json. Remove this whole entry and goods reach the stockpile the moment they are made.
_materials: Carts bring materials to workshops too. A workshop (a building whose production takes inputs) keeps its own store of them, room for 'store' of each, and works only from that. A cart going to a workshop takes materials from the stockpile to fill the store, and comes back with what the workshop made. Needs 'carts'. Remove this entry and workshops take their materials straight from the stockpile.
_trade: The trade ship. While the island has a Harbour linked to a warehouse, a ship calls every 'shipEverySeconds' of game time. On each call it carries at most 'unitsPerHarbor' units for each such Harbour, sold and bought together. What it sells and buys is set by the player in the Harbour's panel. Prices are in goods.json. Remove this whole entry to switch trade off.
_fleet: Your own ship, which carries goods between the home island and the second island. It sails once each island has a Harbour. It carries at most 'capacity' units a trip, sails one tile of sea every 'secondsPerTile', and spends 'loadSeconds' in each harbour. What it carries each way is set in a Harbour's panel. Remove this whole entry and the second island has no ship.
_settlers: Help to settle the second island, in a game that has one: 'grantCoins' given at the win, when it opens, and 'incomePerMinute' added to the base income once it has both a warehouse and a harbour. Remove this entry for neither.
_tradePrices: Prices that move. Each good the trade ship deals in has a price factor, normally 1. Every unit sold to the ship lowers it by 'perUnit', and every unit bought raises it by as much, but it stays between 'lowest' and 'highest'. At each call the pull on the price is first cut to 'keepPerCall' of what it was, so prices drift back to normal. The factor of a call is the one it starts with. Remove this entry for fixed prices.
_win: The win: this many residents of this tier, or of any tier above it.
_milestones: Goals for after the win, in order. Each is reached like the win and shown on the goal bar once the one before it is done.
_addedLater: What has been added to the game since saved games first existed, one entry per round of additions, oldest first. A game saved before any of them can still be continued: it simply has none of what came after. If you add a good, a building or a tier of your own, add an entry at the end and older saved games keep working. 'buildingSettings' names a setting added to buildings, such as 'staff', and 'goodSettings' one added to goods, such as 'trade', 'mapSettings' one added to map.json, such as 'second', 'tierNeeds' a need added to a tier that already existed, as 'tier:good', and 'tierSettings' a setting added to tiers.
